intro: Using context to recognise an indirect criticism and tell it apart from literal praise.
p.ironía.consejo: The accent on the i separates the vowels: i-ro-NÍ-a. You notice it from context and tone.
p.literal.consejo: The opposite of figurative or ironic. «En sentido literal» means «exactly as said».
p.elogio.consejo: It is written with g but sounds like h: e-LO-hyo. The opposite is «la crítica».
p.crítica.consejo: It has an accent on the i: KRÍ-ti-ka. A «crítica» can be good or bad.
p.recorrido.consejo: The rr is strong: rre-ko-RRI-do. It comes from «recorrer».
p.afirmar.consejo: The critic states something and the reader decides whether to believe it. The opposite is «negar».
p.contraste.consejo: It is masculine: «un contraste». It appears when words do not match the facts.
p.exposición.consejo: It ends in -ción: ek-spo-si-THYON. It is also «explaining a topic» in a talk.
p.entre líneas.consejo: You say «leer entre líneas»: understanding what someone suggests without saying it.
p.comodidad.consejo: It comes from «cómodo». It ends in -dad, so the stress is at the end: ko-mo-di-DAD.
b1.titulo: Read the context, not one word alone
b1.texto:
**Ironía** says one thing and suggests another, often the opposite. It shows in the **contraste** between the words and the facts.

If someone praises with exaggeration something that has a flaw, it may not be an **elogio** but a **crítica**. You have to read **entre líneas** and compare the sentence with the details around it.

Not every strong adjective is ironic: you need evidence. That is why it is better not to take everything **literally**, nor to suspect every sentence.
b2.titulo: A review with a hidden edge
b2.f0.texto: Have you seen the new exhibition at the City Museum?
b2.f1.texto: The review says the route is an adventure.
b2.f3.texto: The review adds that there is only one bench in three rooms.
b2.f4.texto: Then the contrast reveals an ironic criticism.
b2.f5.texto: Irony says one thing and suggests another.
b2.f6.texto: You have to read between the lines and look at the facts.
b2.f7.texto: That is why it is not wise to take everything literally.
b4.titulo: Saying one thing and suggesting another
b4.texto:
Some signals help to find irony:

- **Parecer** + noun: what **parece** praise may be something else. **La frase parece un elogio.**
- **En realidad**, **de hecho**: they introduce what the author really means. **En realidad, el autor critica la comodidad.**
- A concrete detail that **contradicts** the fine words: **solo hay un banco en tres salas.**

Irony is not decided by a single word: it relies on the **context**.
b4.e1.texto: In fact, the author criticises the comfort of the route.
b4.e2.texto: Nobody wastes time choosing a seat.
b5.f0.texto: The museum rooms smell of waxed wood and ancient silence.
b5.f1.texto: The visitors' footsteps sound hollow on the wooden floor.
b5.f2.texto: In the display cases rest yellowed letters, blurry photographs and silver spoons.
b5.f3.texto: An elderly woman moves slowly, her bag pressed against her chest.
b5.f4.texto: Every few steps she looks with her eyes for a place to rest.
b5.f5.texto: At the back of the third room a wooden bench finally appears.
b5.f6.texto: It is taken by a guard who reads the newspaper with a calm air.
b5.f7.texto: The visitor smiles, understands and keeps walking towards the next room.
b5.f8.texto: In the last display case, a farewell letter draws a sad smile from her.
b5.f9.texto: On leaving, the air of the street seems to her the best prize of the whole visit.
b6.o0: decir siempre la verdad sin adornos
b6.o0.refuerzo: That is speaking literally, not with irony.
b6.o1: decir una cosa y dar a entender otra
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: irony says something to suggest another, often the opposite.
b6.o2: repetir las palabras de otra persona
b6.o2.refuerzo: Repeating is not irony, although it is sometimes used to be ironic.
b7.frase: La frase parece un elogio, ____ el contexto revela una crítica.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «pero» marks the contrast between what seems and what is.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Porque» gives a cause, not a contrast.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Por ejemplo» introduces an example, not a contrast.
b8.frase: El contraste revela una crítica irónica
b8.traduccion: The contrast reveals an ironic criticism
b9.o0.refuerzo: A single bench suggests the opposite: little comfort.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The text does not say that: it says seats are lacking.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: few benches mean few places to sit.
b9.pregunta: What does a single bench in three rooms suggest?
b11.frase: El crítico ____ que la visita fue cómoda.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «afirmar» is saying that something is true.
b11.o1.refuerzo: «Recorrer» is going through a place, not saying something.
b11.o2.refuerzo: «Contrastar» is comparing two things; it does not take «que» like this.
b11.pregunta: Which verb means to say with certainty?
b12.o0: que la exposición merece la visita
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: despite the flaw, the review recommends the exhibition.
b12.o1.refuerzo: The review praises the materials and the texts.
b12.o2.refuerzo: The bench is a detail, not the overall opinion.
b12.pregunta: What is the final opinion of the review?
p.aventura.consejo: Feminine: «la aventura». The v sounds like «b».
p.revela.consejo: «Revelar» means to make something known. The v sounds like «b».
p.irónica.consejo: Feminine of «irónico». The tilde marks the stress on RO.
p.conviene.consejo: Works like «gustar»: «no conviene» means it is not wise.
p.sentido.consejo: «En sentido literal» means taken word for word.
p.autor.consejo: Feminine: «la autora». The au is one diphthong.
p.critica.consejo: «Criticar» is to criticize. Stress on KRI.
p.eligiendo.consejo: The gerund of «elegir». The g before i sounds like «h».
p.encerada.consejo: From «cera», wax. The c before e sounds like «th».
p.huecos.consejo: The h is silent: WE-kos. Masculine plural.
p.vitrinas.consejo: Feminine plural: «la vitrina». The v sounds like «b».
p.fotografías.consejo: Feminine plural: «la fotografía». The tilde marks the stress on FI.
p.borrosas.consejo: Feminine plural of «borroso». The rr is strong.
p.cucharas.consejo: Feminine plural: «la cuchara». The ch sounds like «ch» in «chair».
p.avanza.consejo: The z sounds like «th» in Spain. The v sounds like «b».
p.guardia.consejo: «El guardia» is masculine. Stress on GWAR, with the g hard.
p.visitante.consejo: Used for men and women: «el visitante», «la visitante».
p.caminando.consejo: Gerund ending in -ando. Used with «seguir»: «sigue caminando».
p.arranca.consejo: «Arrancar una sonrisa» means to draw out a smile.
p.contexto.consejo: Masculine: «el contexto». The x sounds like «ks».
p.sitios.consejo: Masculine plural: «el sitio». Stress on SI.
p.afirma.consejo: «Afirmar» means to state firmly. Stress on FIR.
p.merece.consejo: «Merecer» has the c before e, which sounds like «th».
